chapter_title: [Concerning the Five] War[s that the] Sons of [Li]ght waged with the Sons] of Darkness.
chapter_note: This chapter is largely a core cosmological sequence: five ordered "wars" describing major salvific operations (First Living Man; Living Spirit; Third Ambassador; Jesus the glorious one; Counsel of Life). There is a thin hagiographic dialogue attribution at the opening (¶1), a clear Christian overlay via a Gospel-style citation formula (¶2), and an editorial/pastoral beatitude applying the victory-pattern to the "elect" at the end (¶9), consistent with the chapter’s second-half drift.

paragraphs.core_text: The sons of light waged five wars against the sons of darkness. The sons of light humiliated the sons of darkness in them all.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution/frame formula: "Then the enlightener speaks:" (hagiographic/compilation layer).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching statement is impersonal and cosmological (Light vs. Darkness; fivefold structure), but introduced by a late dialogue attribution marker typical of the Kephalaia frame.

paragraphs.core_text: The first war is that of the First living Man, which he waged against the King of the realms of Darkness, and all the rulers that had come forth from the five worlds of [...]. He hunted them with his net, which is the living soul. He [...] in the snare and [...] the face of the [...] his virgin, the living fire [...] they did not find how to escape his net [...] he caught them like fish [...] the five counsels of the five elements [...]. He cut and dug out the root of the five trees, [...] root of the evil tree, like an axe.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed Christian overlay/citation formula and quoted Gospel-like saying: "As the saviour has said: Behold, the axe is put to the root of the evil tree..." (entered via NT/Gospel tradition).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core layer is systematic cosmological mechanism (First Living Man’s net = living soul; rulers from five worlds; five elements/counsels; tree-root imagery as internal correspondence). The final line shifts to explicit Gospel-style authority citation ("As the saviour has said"), marking later Christian overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: The second war is that of the Living Spirit [...]. He has constructed the things and the worlds of light; he spread out the rulers and chained them in the middle [...] the stars in [...] the earths [...] them in the three vessels. For the rulers rebelled and were set against the Living Spirit. They wished to [...] since they knew and realised that he might bind and fetter them with a strong chain. Yet he, the Living Spirit, (appeared to them) with many aspects, with numerous [...], with many hands and great cruelties. He was revealed to them, he imprisoned them with much skill. Not one of them was able to save (himself), and he [...] [...]. Now, since he [...] he trapped them [...] [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, process-oriented cosmological exposition (construction of worlds; chaining rulers; three vessels). No institutional pointing or citation; reads as core teaching. Page marker and curly-brace artifact removed from extraction per rules.

paragraphs.core_text: The third war is that of the Third Ambassador who has displayed his image [...] what is below [...] scooped [...] all light and the property [...] the ones that are consumed [...] the entire ruling-power [...] pride of the light [...] extending it [...]. A person comes, who is powerful [...]; he takes his riches [...], silver [...], his pride and wantonness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-agent operation (Third Ambassador; image-display; extraction of Light) with a short illustrative parable-like turn that remains explanatory, not institutional—typical of core correspondential pedagogy.

paragraphs.core_text: This is what the ruling-power is like [...], all riches [...] as they travel [...] light [...]. He cleansed and purified it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation/conclusion of the illustrative comparison about the ruling-power and the purification of Light; remains within the cosmological mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth war is this that Jesus the glorious one waged against all the rebels who had rebelled above and below. When the light was purified from them by the image of the Third Ambassador, their chains loosened [...]. The glorious one in the fourth war; he came and brought [...] a rebellion of the entire ruling-power. He girded himself [...] all of it another time. He constructed the whole structure and he made [...] a great contest; he humiliated therein. [...] he fulfilled the will of the greatness, [he gave the] hope to Adam [...] to his light ship.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus appears as a defined cosmological actor in the Manichaean hierarchy (not a Gospel citation). The paragraph stays cosmos→cosmos (rebels; chains; structure; Adam’s enlightenment/hope), with no NT quotation formula.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth war is this that the counsel of life [...] which is the summons and the obedience [...] great [...] and it placed [...] upon the [...] and the [...] [...] of death, which [...] with it. And it was victorious over [...] for ever, and it gave the kingdom [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological/cosmic completion act (Counsel of Life; Summons and Obedience) expressed in structural terms; page marker removed per rules.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the good are victorious over the wicked [...] for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief summarizing dualist maxim consistent with the closure of a five-war cosmological victory sequence; no institutional or citation markers.

Direct beatitude addressed to the community using institutional category "elect" and application language (blessedness for persons who imitate the five wars). This is cosmos→community pointing, characteristic of late pastoral/application grafting.
